title: The second reader, for the subsystems it covers -- 28 of 37 durable actions
note: R42 and R53 said the same thing from two directions: only authority records and tasks had an independent reconstruction, so the scheduler, policy, capability, agent, memory, network, secret and context projections were compared against a fresh replay of THEMSELVES -- which shares their reducer and therefore cannot see a shared misunderstanding. Every mutation here either makes the second reader agree with a forged history (so the differential check agrees with the attacker) or blinds it to a subsystem entirely (so it agrees by covering nothing, which is the quieter failure). R18-R24 attack the ownership and attempt-accounting rules. Before they existed the reader checked only the SHAPE of a transition -- job exists, src matches, not a revival -- and applied the payload verbatim, so it accepted a strictly wider language than the production reducer. That is the worst place for the gap to be: a log the primary refuses cannot be loaded, the two readers are never compared, and the permissive one is the only reader left. R29-R40 attack the escalation rules. Until they existed this reader had no escalation reconstruction at all, while the campaign was described as covering the second reader for EVERY subsystem -- two statements that could not both be true.

mutations.name: D1_a_job_may_be_born_in_any_state
mutations.rationale: the second reader accepts a job born SUCCEEDED or DISPATCHED, so the differential check confirms a forged outcome instead of contradicting it

mutations.name: D2_the_initial_job_states_include_a_terminal_one
mutations.rationale: a job that was never run is projected as having succeeded

mutations.name: D3_the_submitter_comes_from_the_payload
mutations.rationale: a forged enqueue is attributed to whoever it names, and separation of duties is measured from that field

mutations.name: D4_a_job_may_be_enqueued_holding_a_lease
mutations.rationale: the enqueue supplies the ownership precondition its own outcome edges will check

mutations.name: D5_a_forged_source_state_is_accepted
mutations.find:
if cur["state"] != src:
        _note(out, ev, f"job {jid!r} claims src {src!r} but replay has it "
mutations.replace:
if False:
        _note(out, ev, f"job {jid!r} claims src {src!r} but replay has it "
mutations.rationale: the record chooses the state it is authorized against, which is the forged-source-state class this project has already been bitten by

mutations.name: D6_a_terminal_job_may_be_revived
mutations.rationale: a finished job is walked back into the queue and re-run, which is how a completed outcome gets replaced

mutations.name: D7_a_capability_may_predate_its_own_record
mutations.rationale: a grant appended late reads as authority in force over everything that already happened

mutations.name: D8_a_capability_id_may_be_reissued
mutations.find:
_note(out, ev, f"capability {cid!r} is issued twice with different "
                       "terms; two grants sharing an id cannot be told apart")
        return
mutations.replace:
out.capabilities[cid] = {"capability_id": cid, "subject": p.get("subject"), "action": p.get("action"), "task_id": p.get("task_id"), "tool_id": p.get("tool_id"), "scope": tuple(p.get("scope") or ()), "issued_seq": issued, "expires_after_seq": p.get("expires_after_seq"), "revoked_seq": None, "body": {k: v for k, v in p.items() if k != "task_id"}}
        return
mutations.rationale: a live grant is replaced by one nobody reviewed, and anything citing the id now cites the replacement

mutations.name: D9_an_agent_may_mint_a_human
mutations.find:
if kind == "HUMAN" and registrar is not None and \
            registrar.get("kind") != "HUMAN":
mutations.rationale: the second reader accepts an invented human, so the confederate that answers the escalation looks legitimate to both readers

mutations.name: D10_a_memory_entry_names_its_own_author
mutations.rationale: a note is attributed to whoever the payload names, and authorship is what a conflict comparison rests on

mutations.name: D11_a_retracted_memory_may_be_revived
mutations.rationale: a withdrawn note is un-withdrawn by a forged event; the author never really withdrew it

mutations.name: D12_a_malformed_memory_write_is_projected_anyway
mutations.find:
if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        _note(out, ev, "memory.write carries no entry; a record this reader "
mutations.replace:
if False:
        _note(out, ev, "memory.write carries no entry; a record this reader "
mutations.rationale: the reader crashes or silently skips on the payload shape that once made a whole store unloadable with a raw KeyError

mutations.name: D13_a_grant_id_may_be_rebound
mutations.find:
_note(out, ev, f"{what} grant {gid!r} is re-issued with different "
                       "terms; the live grant would be replaced by one "
                       "nobody reviewed")
        return
mutations.replace:
table[gid] = {"grant_id": gid, "digest": p.get("grant_digest"), "issued_seq": ev.seq, "revoked_seq": None, "body": grant}
        return
mutations.rationale: an egress or secret grant is silently repointed at another host, and both readers now agree it always pointed there

mutations.name: D14_a_policy_downgrade_is_accepted_silently
mutations.find:
if versions and version is not None and \
            versions[-1]["version"] is not None and \
            version < versions[-1]["version"]:
mutations.rationale: a superseded rule set is republished and answers questions about the range it was already replaced over

mutations.name: D15_the_comparison_reports_nothing
mutations.find:
if got != want:
                    out.append(Divergence(f"{name}/{key}", fld, want, got))
mutations.replace:
if False:
                    out.append(Divergence(f"{name}/{key}", fld, want, got))
mutations.rationale: the differential check can no longer fail, which makes every agreement it reports meaningless

mutations.name: D16_the_comparison_ignores_a_missing_subsystem
mutations.rationale: an object one reader holds and the other does not stops being a divergence, so a forged record that only reaches one projection is invisible

mutations.name: D17_the_second_reader_skips_the_scheduler_entirely
mutations.rationale: the reader agrees by covering nothing, which is the quieter failure: an empty second projection diffs clean against anything

mutations.name: R18_the_reader_does_not_ask_who_signed_an_outcome
mutations.find:
if cur.get("lease_holder") != ev.actor:
            _note(out, ev, f"job {jid!r} is held by "
mutations.replace:
if False:
            _note(out, ev, f"job {jid!r} is held by "
mutations.rationale: the second reader projects a verdict written by somebody who was not running the work. The primary refuses such a log outright, so the two readers are never compared on it -- this reader is the only one looking

mutations.name: R19_the_reader_accepts_an_outcome_after_possession_ran_out
mutations.find:
if not holds:
            _note(out, ev, f"job {jid!r} had possession only to seq {end!r} "
mutations.replace:
if False:
            _note(out, ev, f"job {jid!r} had possession only to seq {end!r} "
mutations.rationale: a worker back from the dead decides an outcome for work that may already have been redone, and the independent reconstruction agrees with it

mutations.name: R20_the_reader_lets_a_live_lease_be_reclaimed
mutations.find:
if (src == "DISPATCHED" and dst in {"READY", "FAILED"}
            and cur.get("lease_holder") != ev.actor and holds):
mutations.rationale: the handover edges are guarded by the fact they assert. Drop the check and a record claiming a lapse that did not happen replays clean

mutations.name: R21_the_reader_takes_the_attempt_count_from_the_payload
mutations.find: allowed = have + 1 if charge else have
mutations.rationale: the count the retry budget is measured against becomes whatever the record says it is, so an independently reconstructed history shows a budget that never runs down

mutations.name: R22_the_reader_lets_a_transition_grant_possession
mutations.find: if grants and not (src == "READY" and dst == "DISPATCHED"):
mutations.rationale: ownership is taken at hand-out and dropped on the way back. Allow any edge to carry it and a record names its own owner

mutations.name: R23_the_reader_judges_possession_where_the_record_LANDED
mutations.find:
holds = bool(cur.get("lease_id")) and isinstance(end, int) and (
        (ev.seq - 1) <= end)
mutations.replace:
holds = bool(cur.get("lease_id")) and isinstance(end, int) and (
        ev.seq <= end)
mutations.rationale: off by one in the direction that FAILS CLOSED, which is why it would survive a test written in the comfortable middle: a report decided at the last legal position lands one past it and is refused as late. The second reader would report an anomaly against an entirely honest log

mutations.name: R24_the_reader_does_not_carry_the_retry_budget
mutations.find:
budget = job.get("max_attempts")
    if isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
mutations.rationale: an enqueue that states no bound is accepted silently, and the count in the reconstruction has nothing to be measured against

mutations.name: R25_the_reader_takes_the_submitter_from_the_payload
mutations.rationale: the primary refuses a create naming a submitter it is not, so such a log never reaches compare_tasks. A silent second reader leaves nothing in the system saying anything about the forgery

mutations.name: R26_the_reader_lets_anyone_revoke_a_capability
mutations.find: if ev.actor != cur.get("issued_by") and ev.actor != out.root_issuer:
mutations.rationale: the mint side of this reader asks whether the actor could create the grant; without this, nothing asks whether it could destroy one

mutations.name: R27_the_reader_lets_anyone_revoke_a_grant
mutations.rationale: for secret grants this reader is not a second opinion but the only one -- SecretStore has no reducer, so nothing else re-reads such a record

mutations.name: R28_the_reader_lets_anyone_retire_a_human
mutations.rationale: this reader refuses an agent that ADMITS a human and would accept one that removes every human there is

mutations.name: R29_the_reader_does_not_check_who_raised_it
mutations.rationale: an escalation is attributed to whoever asked it; without this an agent opens one in a person's name, which is false attribution and also stops that person answering, since the raiser may not

mutations.name: R30_the_reader_accepts_an_escalation_born_answered
mutations.rationale: a question born ANSWERED was never asked and carries a decision nobody is recorded as having made

mutations.name: R31_the_reader_accepts_a_question_with_one_answer
mutations.rationale: an answer that cannot be checked against what was asked is a conversation, not a decision

mutations.name: R32_the_reader_lets_an_escalation_be_raised_twice
mutations.rationale: the second record replaces a question somebody may already have answered

mutations.name: R33_the_reader_lets_a_decided_escalation_be_decided_again
mutations.rationale: a recorded human decision is rewritten by a later record, and terminality is what makes an answer worth anything

mutations.name: R34_the_reader_does_not_ask_who_signed_the_answer
mutations.rationale: every check after this one interrogates answered_by, so without it they all pass on a borrowed name and an agent signs a person's decision

mutations.name: R35_the_reader_lets_a_non_human_answer
mutations.rationale: the strongest claim the directory makes -- no arrangement of roles substitutes for a person -- goes unchecked in the reader that exists to check it independently

mutations.name: R36_the_reader_lets_the_asker_answer_their_own
mutations.rationale: the party who could not decide decides, which is the whole of what an escalation is for

mutations.name: R37_the_reader_accepts_an_answer_outside_the_options
mutations.rationale: a free-text answer to a closed question cannot be checked against what was asked

mutations.name: R38_the_reader_lets_anyone_withdraw
mutations.rationale: a third party retires a question somebody was waiting on, and a withdrawal claims no human decided anything so nothing else would notice

mutations.name: R39_the_reader_lets_a_retired_human_answer
mutations.rationale: a principal that has left the project is still the person a decision is attributed to

mutations.name: R40_the_reader_accepts_a_state_that_is_neither
mutations.rationale: an escalation is moved to a state that is neither answered nor withdrawn, and the terminality checks above then have nothing to bite on
